items.stem: What is the clearest distinction between internationalization (i18n) and localization (l10n)?

options.text: i18n prepares the product to support many locales; l10n adapts it to a specific locale
options.rationale: Correct: i18n is the engineering groundwork, l10n is the per-locale adaptation such as translation.

options.text: i18n means translating strings; l10n means writing code
options.rationale: This reverses the roles; translation is part of l10n.

options.text: i18n applies only to right-to-left languages
options.rationale: i18n applies to all locales, not only RTL ones.

items.explanation: Correct: i18n is the engineering groundwork, l10n is the per-locale adaptation such as translation.

items.stem: Which TWO practices correctly support a right-to-left layout? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use CSS logical properties such as margin-inline-start instead of margin-left
options.rationale: Correct: logical properties flip automatically with text direction.

options.text: Set the dir attribute so the browser lays out bidi text correctly
options.rationale: Correct: the dir attribute drives bidirectional layout and text direction.

options.text: Hard-code every margin to the left side
options.rationale: Fixed left-side margins do not flip for RTL and break the layout.

options.text: Mirror all icons including directional-neutral ones like a clock
options.rationale: Neutral icons such as a clock must not be mirrored; only direction-dependent icons like a back arrow flip.

items.explanation: Correct: logical properties flip automatically with text direction.

items.stem: A translated German label is 40% longer than the English original and overflows its button. What is the best fix?

options.text: Design the layout to accommodate text expansion with flexible sizing
options.rationale: Correct: allowing for text expansion is a core i18n layout requirement.

options.text: Forbid translations longer than the English text
options.rationale: Languages legitimately expand; forbidding it would mistranslate content.

options.text: Shrink the font until any text fits
options.rationale: Arbitrary shrinking harms readability and accessibility.
Silent truncation loses meaning and is a defect, not a fix.

items.explanation: Correct: allowing for text expansion is a core i18n layout requirement.
